how: Tokyo gets almost no lasting snow, so snow sculpting is not possible locally; the nearest large-scale venue is the Sapporo Snow Festival in Hokkaido, about 1.5 hours by air.
FabCafe Tokyo in Shibuya offers digital fabrication including 3D printing and laser cutting to visitors.
FabCafe Tokyo's MTRL workspace in Shibuya offers prototyping and digital fabrication machines and materials.
Game jams and developer study events are regularly listed on connpass for Tokyo venues.
Hobby fireworks making is not available: manufacturing explosives requires licences under Japan's explosives control law, so fireworks are made only by licensed professional makers.
University clubs such as Tokyo Tech's CREATE rocketry club build and launch rockets near Tokyo, and occasional public model rocket workshops run in the Kanagawa area.
Maker Faire Tokyo and maker spaces such as FabCafe support electronics, Arduino and Raspberry Pi projects, and Akihabara is Japan's electronics parts district.

how: Tokyo Tabletop, a Meetup-based group, hosts weekly tabletop gaming sessions in Shibuya including roleplaying games.
Mahjong parlours (jansou) are common across Tokyo, and the Japan Professional Mahjong Association is based in the city.
TELL Pub Quiz runs a regular English-language quiz night in Tokyo, held at the Footnik pub in Osaki.
Green Bean to Bar Chocolate in Nakameguro makes chocolate from the bean and has run workshops on the production process.

how: Home bakeries in Tokyo run bread and shokupan baking classes for visitors via booking platforms such as ByFood and Rakuten Experiences.
Natural-yeast bread classes are offered by home bakeries in Setagaya through Rakuten Experiences.
Hitachino Brewing Lab near Akihabara offers hands-on beer classes alongside its taproom, while home brewing is limited by Japanese alcohol-tax rules.
The Nippon Bartenders Association is based in Tokyo and the city has a dense cocktail bar scene, including Ginza bars.
Home coffee-roasting experiences are offered by former baristas in Ota City, Tokyo, via Airbnb Experiences.
Toshimaya Brewery in Musashimurayama, western Tokyo, offers guided tours of its sake production with tastings, but hands-on brewing is not confirmed for the public.
Toshimaya Brewery, founded 1596 in western Tokyo, runs guided tours ending with sake tastings, and Tokyo has many sake bars.
Tokyo has many beginner sushi-making classes, including sessions tied to Tsukiji fish market where participants make nigiri and maki with a professional chef.
Fermentation is central to Japanese food and sake brewery tours exist, but a regular kombucha or kimchi class is not confirmed.
Tokyo is a major vinyl market with large record-store districts such as Shibuya and Shinjuku, home to chains like Disk Union.
Tokyo English Book Exchange and similar groups meet in Shibuya to swap and discuss English books.
Tokyo Writers Workshop meets monthly in English to critique fiction and poetry, and Tokyo Poetry Journal lists creative writing workshops.
Tokyo Poetry Journal (ToPoJo) lists poetry readings and events at Tokyo venues.
Language exchange and English book-swap meetups run regularly in Tokyo.
Toastmasters International lists English and Japanese clubs across Tokyo.
The University of Tokyo and other Tokyo universities hold public lectures and symposia for general audiences.
Tokyo has large Meetup-based communities, such as Tokyo Tabletop with over 4,000 members, plus connpass events.
HOUYHNHNM Running Club runs a running station in Nihonbashi Hamacho with Sumida River routes.
Toshimaen Niwa-no-yu in Meguro and other Tokyo saunas and sento provide cold plunge pools.
